description:
## Question

For each target workload (WebSocket masking, PCM mixing with clip prevention, HLL updates, cosine top-k over f32, batched Levenshtein, Gorilla encoding), sketch a rough kernel the way an Elixir developer writes it first, starting from the anchor package's own Elixir code. The sketch doesn't need to compile against defk today. Collect every convenience construct the sketches reach for (candidates: |>, Enum.sum/max/min over arrays, indexed generators, module attributes as constants, for ... into: an allocated array, multi-clause kernels, <<>> matching on fixed fields, the <<bits::64>> = <<x::float-64>> match form) and decide which are in the kernel subset. A construct is in only if it is what an Elixir developer writes first, costs nothing over the hand loop, and keeps Elixir's meaning; types and bit output are already decided.

Output: the sketches linked as a prototype asset; per construct in/out with the workloads that need it; one roadmap ticket per accepted construct (each needs an Elixir-mode meaning, agreement tests and a docs/language.md entry). Workload tickets may still add constructs later.

comments.text:
Resolution:
- Sketches: branch prototype/defk-dtw.18-sketches, prototypes/convenience_sketches.exs (throwaway, never merged). Each starts from the anchor package's Elixir code and tags the constructs it reaches for.
- In: module attributes as constants (integer/float, inlined; PCM, Gorilla, masks) -> [Module attributes as constants in kernels](defk-ivt); multi-clause kernels with a bodiless typed head and case-style patterns plus guards (Gorilla dod buckets) -> [Multi-clause kernels with a typed function head](defk-u9c); signed segments v::k-signed in the bitstring accumulator, out-of-range raises (Gorilla) -> [Signed integer segments in the bitstring accumulator](defk-dki); the accumulator passed to and returned from helper kernels, still append-only, never an entry input (Gorilla) -> [Pass the bitstring accumulator through helper kernels](defk-ooq). Bitwise operator forms (&&& >>> ^^^; HLL, Gorilla, masking) were already in [Support bitwise operators in kernels](defk-w38).
- Out (with a targeted compile-error hint, commented on defk-vku): |> (no sketch used it); Enum.sum/min/max/min_by/min_max (every use was over a slice or expression, never a whole array; the reduce loop is the form); indexed generators and for ... into:; <<>> fixed-field matching (indexed reads instead); <<b::64>> = <<x::float-64>> (Defk.Bits.f64_to_u64/1); Enum.min/max over a list literal (nested min/2).
- PCM's data-dependent output length needs no construct: return {out, count, held, sign}, caller takes binary_part (zero-copy).
- A write to a parameter array that is never returned (PCM emit_wave trap) becomes a compile error; commented on [Give arrays value semantics: copy on aliased write](defk-auo).
- Gorilla's anchor mask (1 <<< len) - 1 overflows i64 at len 64: a limit, hint on defk-vku.
- Wiring: defk-ivt blocks PCM (defk-9p6.14) and Gorilla (defk-9p6.16); defk-u9c, defk-dki, defk-ooq block Gorilla; defk-cmr blocks defk-dki and defk-ooq. Workload tickets may still add constructs.

title: Which convenience constructs do the six target workloads need?
